I am an old man. I farm 3 mu — small land, just me and my wife. I do what I have always done, what my neighbors do. I will tell you how I think.

**Wheat first.** I plant winter wheat in October, like always. I buy seed from the village shop — the new kind everyone buys now, not the old seed. For 3 mu I need maybe 40 jin of seed (about 10 kg per mu).

Before planting I put down compound fertilizer — the 15-15-15 bag, what we call "three fifteens." One bag is 50 kg. For my 3 mu I use 6 bags, so 2 bags per mu, 100 kg. That is what the dealer says and what my neighbor does. Then in spring when the wheat greens up and I turn on the well, I spread urea — one bag per mu, 50 kg. Urea is cheap and the wheat needs it, or the leaves turn yellow and the ear stays small. I have seen that happen.

I plough the field with the small tractor I hire from the village — 40 yuan per mu. My father ploughed with an ox, but now everyone uses the tractor. I water the wheat 4 times from the well — before winter so it does not freeze dry, then green-up in March, then when the ear comes out, then when the grain fills. If I skip water the wheat shrinks.

For spray, I do it twice — once against the wheat aphid when they come in April, once against weeds early. If I see rust I spray again but usually twice is enough. I expect 900 jin per mu — 450 kg. A good year, maybe 950. Bad year, 800.

**Then maize.** After wheat harvest in June I plant maize right away. No time to waste, no ploughing — the machine sows straight into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed, the one the shop recommends. I use 2 bags of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing through the machine, then I topdress urea at knee-high stage, about 1 bag per mu. Maize eats a lot — if I am stingy the cobs are small.

Well water twice for maize — once after sowing if no rain, once when it tassels. Summer rain usually helps. Spray once for the corn borer, maybe twice if bugs are bad. I expect 1100 jin per mu — 550 kg. 

I would rather buy a little extra fertilizer than lose half my grain. Fertilizer is money, but an empty granary is a disaster.
